senses.gloss:
Kautasta, a word occurring once in the dual, is apparently a patronymic of arimejaya and janamejaya, two adhvaryu priests at the snake sacrifice described in the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes xxv. 15, 3. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 35.

Kautsa (‘descendant of Kutsa’) is mentioned in the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa as a pupil of māhitthi. A kautsa is also attacked in the nirukta as denying the value of the Vedas, and there is a strong ritual tradition of hostility to the Kautsas.
Foot notes x. 6, 5, 9; Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad, vi. 5, 4 (kāṇva recension only).
i. 15.
E.g., Āpastamba śrauta sūtra, x. 20, 12; Hillebrandt, Vedische Mythologie, 3, 285. Cf. Weber, Indian Literature, 77, 140.

Kautsī-putra (‘son of a female descendant of kutsa’) is mentioned as a pupil of baudhīputra in the last vaṃśa (list of teachers) of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad in the Mādhyaṃdina recension (vi. 4, 31).
